text:
incident-bot: Paging: smart-routing.alert - Region fallback loop detected between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Multiple fallback transitions in last 2m. Auto-escalation to on-call. :rotating_light:

emma: I'm on it. Seeing repeated health-check flips: us-east health=healthy -> failing -> healthy -> failing in <30s windows. 5xx spike and latency increase for routes using smart-routing-v3.

kevin: @emma any impact to enterprise customers?

emma: Initial metrics: ~12% of requests experienced >500ms and ~0.7% 5xx for affected model routes. Two customers with reserved Dedicated pools saw degraded P95.

raj: tagging for visibility. I'll join for handoff in 10. What's current mitigation plan?

emma: First step: stop the automatic region fallback loop by temporarily setting fallback_cooldown to 120s and disable multi-hop fallback. Will pin policy to prefer single-step failover. Doing via control-plane API now.

emma: Command I'm running: 
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/routing/policy/smart-routing-v3/actions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"action":"update","changes":{"fallback_cooldown":120,"multi_hop_fallback":false}}'
```

ops-bot: action accepted. Policy smart-routing-v3 updated by emma at 1782105720.

kevin: Good. That should stop flip-flop. Can we also reduce health-check sensitivity from check_fail_threshold=2 -> 4 to avoid transient transient alerts?

emma: Yes. Planning to increase check_fail_threshold to 4 for region health-checks and add a 10s jitter. Applying now.

emma: Command: 
```
rwctl infra update-healthcheck --region all --check-fail-threshold 4 --jitter 10s
```

ops-bot: healthcheck update job queued (job_id: hj-3221).

incident-bot: Noted: customer-impact flag set to "partial-degradation". Pager duty escalation level: P1->P0? recommendation: remain P1 until stabilization.

kevin: Keep P1. We'll only promote to P0 if service-level outage confirmed.

lucy: FYI: I put a block in the routing overlay to stop eu <-> us-west automatic fallback for 5m as a safety measure. That prevents the loop while we stabilize.

emma: Command run: 
```
rwctl routing block-add --from eu --to us-west --duration 5m --reason "loop mitigation"
```

ops-bot: routing block applied (blk-881).

cs-team-bot: Notifying impacted customers: IDs cust-1287, cust-3429, cust-9002. Draft sent: "We are investigating intermittent latency and have applied mitigations; we'll update in 15m."

kevin: Any evidence this was caused by wrong model variant routing? e.g., fallback to a larger model variant causing timeouts?

emma: I checked model routing logs. The fallback chain was to compatible model variants, not wrong architecture. Looks like the health-check probe threshold was too tight combined with transient infra flakiness in us-east, which triggered rapid fallback, then the eu region health-check saw the traffic spike and tripped, bouncing back and causing the cycle.

raj: I'll take primary on-call in 12. Emma, can you prepare a short handoff note with what you changed and current metrics?

emma: Handoff note: 
- Changes: smart-routing-v3 fallback_cooldown=120s, multi_hop_fallback=false, health-check threshold=4, routing block eu->us-west 5m.
- Why: prevent multi-region rapid fallback loop caused by aggressive health-checks + capacity ripple.
- Current metrics (1782105750): error rate down from 0.7% -> 0.25%, median latency down 120ms -> 70ms. Requests affected ~6% now.
- Next steps: monitor 15m, run canary traffic to bring eu back to safe load.

ops-bot: emma marked status: mitigations_applied.

raj: Taking over. @emma thanks. I'll keep the block for 5m and then slowly re-enable eu->us-west with rate cap.

raj: Plan to re-enable with a staged ramp: allow 5% cross-region fallback for 5m -> 15% for 10m -> 100% if stable. Will set circuit-breaker on fallback_count > 6/min.

emma: Sounds good. Also recommend a follow-up to change default health-check config for smart-routing: increase fail threshold and add cooldown to prevent future loops. Add to postmortem.

kevin: Also file a short RCA with timeline and customer impact. Assign to emma/raj to own.

lucy: Quick note: there was an overlapping deploy of autoscaler agent in us-east ~1782105605, might have contributed to brief resource jitter. Noted in postmortem.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler-agent v2.4.1 deployed to us-east at 1782105605 by kevin.

cs-team-bot: Customer update sent: next update at +30m.

raj: Monitoring dashboards show steady improvement. Keeping channel open for 30m and will close when P95 and 5xx return to baseline.

emma: Action items logged: 
- emma: push routing policy default changes to repo (PR) 
- raj: implement circuit-breaker for fallback_count 
- lucy: correlate autoscaler deploy metrics with health-check spikes 
- kevin: update customer communications if escalation needed

kevin: Thanks all. If anything flares, call me directly. :phone:

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied. Monitor state for 30m before declaring resolved.

raj: Marking handoff complete. I'll post a follow-up summary with timestamps and links to dashboards.

emma: Thanks team.
